title: apex.competition.v1
description: Declarative, versioned description of an Apex competition. Validated platform-side by the spec syncer before an image is mirrored or a spec is activated. Stored as YAML in the apex-competitions-registry repo.

id.description: Stable competition id. Matches the registry folder and the DB competition_id key. Lowercase snake_case.

version.description: Semantic version of THIS spec. (id, version) is immutable once synced.

kind.description: solo -> the miner submission runs in its own player sandbox(es) + a referee (a 1-player duel); one player sandbox by default, or N isolated sandboxes of the SAME submission via the optional `solo.player_sandboxes`. duel -> N player sandboxes of DIFFERENT submissions + a referee. Both isolate the miner submission (player) from the scorer (referee).

process_type.description: Scheduling hint. gpu specs are gated by the platform GPU opt-in pool.

cpu_limit.description: Per-sandbox CPU cores. Must not exceed the per-env ceiling (stage 2, prod 4).

mem_limit.description: Per-sandbox memory as a k8s quantity (e.g. 1.5Gi, 512Mi). Floor 256Mi; ceiling stage 2Gi / prod 4Gi.

gpu_count.description: GPUs per sandbox. Must be 0 unless process_type is gpu and the env has a GPU pool.

image.description: The player image (kind: solo runs this alone). Pinned by digest; tags are forbidden.

artifact_type.description: How the platform writes the miner's submission. code=raw source bytes, torchscript=.pt bytes, onnx=.onnx bytes.

target_path.description: Absolute path inside the sandbox where the platform writes the artifact. The image entrypoint loads it.

input_schema.description: JSON Schema for the round input data. Either an inline schema or a $ref to a sibling file (resolved by the SDK / syncer).

screening.description: Layer-1 screening config for the GENERIC platform screener (no competition code). Optional — sensible defaults apply. Keyed by submission.artifact_type: `code` uses the ASTGuard knobs, `torchscript`/`onnx` use the weights-validator knobs. Forbidden-lists are a tripwire, not the boundary (the sandbox is the actual defense), so it is fine that they are visible in the spec.

max_size_mb.description: Reject submissions larger than this (code and model).

extra_forbidden_modules.description: code: modules banned on top of the base ASTGuard set.

extra_forbidden_calls.description: code: bare calls banned on top of the base set.

extra_forbidden_attr_calls.description: code: attribute calls (e.g. os.open) banned on top of the base set.

extra_forbidden_dunder_attrs.description: code: dunder attributes banned on top of the base set.

extra_forbidden_attr_access.description: code: attribute accesses (e.g. sys.modules) to block.

min_weight_bytes.description: model: minimum total tensor-weight bytes (rejects zero-weight heuristics).

max_code_weight_ratio.description: model: max code:weight size ratio (rejects logic-in-code exploits).

defaults.description: Eval and scheduling parameters the worker/scheduler need to run a round. Travel with the spec version. Does NOT include incentive_weight (that is a platform / alpha-voting concern).

evaluate.description: How the PLAYER sandbox (the miner submission) is run. For BOTH solo and duel the submission runs as an isolated HTTP server that the referee reaches over the per-job network — it never shares a sandbox with the scorer.

network_disabled.description: Default false: players must be reachable by the referee on the per-job network.

allow_internet.description: Almost always false. Egress is blocked by the sandbox regardless of network_disabled.

http_api.description: The HTTP server the player sandbox exposes for the referee to drive. Required for both solo and duel.

protocol.description: Must match `referee.protocol`. gym_v1 = the standard /health,/reset,/act API; custom = a competition-defined HTTP API the referee speaks.

generate_round.description: Optional. Image-driven round generation; writes tasks to output_file.

convert_model.description: Optional. Post-round artifact conversion (e.g. .pt -> .onnx). Replaces the bespoke ONNX conversion job.

screen.description: Optional Layer-2 BEHAVIOURAL screener (bespoke checks beyond the generic Layer-1). Runs in its OWN image so secret checks stay private while the player image can be public. The submission is written to submission.target_path and the round input is provided the same way as evaluate; exit 0 = pass, non-zero = fail.

referee.description: The competition-owned scorer sandbox — REQUIRED for both solo and duel (a solo eval is a 1-player duel). Holds the game engine + scoring; the platform drives the player(s) through it. The referee image runs by the convention entrypoint /app/referee.py.

protocol.description: gym_v1 enforces the standard player HTTP API (/health,/reset,/act). custom lets the referee speak any HTTP the players expose; the platform only provisions the network and waits for result.json. Must match entrypoints.evaluate.http_api.protocol.

image.description: The referee/scorer image. Pinned by digest; mirrored + cosign-verified at sync time like the player image.

solo.description: Optional, solo only. Overrides the default single player sandbox. The platform provisions `player_sandboxes` isolated sandboxes, each running a fresh copy of the SAME submission (its own memory and filesystem, no shared state), and injects that many PLAYER_URLS into the referee in canonical order. Use when the evaluation must run distinct phases of one submission in mutually-isolated processes — e.g. a compressor sandbox and a decompressor sandbox that must not pass state to each other. Omit for the usual 1-sandbox solo. Forbidden for duel (use `duel.players_per_match`).

player_sandboxes.description: Number of isolated sandboxes the single submission is mounted into. Default 1 (omit the block). >1 gives the referee that many PLAYER_URLS for the same submission with no shared state between them; NUM_PLAYERS is set to match.

duel.description: Required when kind is duel — the match structure only (the scorer lives in the shared `referee` block). Omitted for solo, which is 1 player / 1 game unless `solo.player_sandboxes` requests more isolated sandboxes of the same submission.

swap_sides.description: If true, the platform reorders PLAYER_URLS across games to cancel first-mover advantage.

signature.description: Keyless cosign identity the platform verifies the image signature against at sync time.

ref.description: Registry image repository WITHOUT a tag (tags are forbidden; pin by digest).

digest.description: Immutable image digest. This is what the platform mirrors and pins.
